Sri.G.T.Kenche Gowda Advocate for Respondent No.1-Sri.Shashidhar advocate for Respondent No.2-Sri.Ravi S.Samprathi
JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.20 lakhs for the death of N.Hemanth Kumar caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 30-1-2021 at about 7.30 a.m. when Hemanth Kumar was walking on the side of extreme Bangalore-Mysore road in front of fire service station, at Ramanagaram town at that time, driver of the gods carrier/Eicher vehicle bearing No.KA-09-D-8333 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Hemanth Kumar, as a result of which, Hemanth Kumar sustained injuries and shifted to Rajiv Gandhi hospital of chest diseases, Bangalore and simultaneously treated at NIMHANS and continued the treatment a Rajiv Gandhi hospital and also at Sanjaya Gandhi hospital, due to multiple injuries died at Bowring hospital on 7-2-2021.

entities.text: Rajiv Gandhi hospital of chest diseases,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is further stated that Hemanth Kumar was unmarried person and on the date of accident, he was working at Narayana Olympiad school, Bangalore as a hostel warden and earning Rs.29,000/-p.m. and petitioners dependent on the income of Hemanth Kumar.
Hence petitioners prays to award compensation of rs.20 lakhs from the respondents.

3. Inspite of due service of notice to the respondents, respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through their respective counsel and filed their respective written statement.

4. The respondent No.1 filed written statement wherein contended that driver of the Eicher goods vehicle was not responsible for the accident and he possessed valid driving licence to drive the vehicle and the vehicle was insured with the 2nd respondent.
The respondent No.1 has already forwarded the documents DL, insurance certificate and RC to the respondent No.2.

If at all any claim is established by the petitioners, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the same as the vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and no liability can be fastended on this respondent.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
5. The respondent No.2 filed written statement wherein contended that petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either on facts or in law against this respondent.
The respondent No.1 has violated the Section 134(c) ad 158(6) of MV Act.
The driver of Eicher was not holding valid and effective DL at the time of accident.

The first respondent has handed over the possession of the Eicher to the said driver and therefore, has contravened the proviso of MV Act and rules framed there under and have committed the beach of the terms and conditions of the policy willfully,
intentionally and consciously.
The Eicher in question did not held valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.

This respondent has issued a policy of insurance in favour of first respondent in respect of Eicher bearing No.KA-09-D-8333, the liability of this respondent company if any is Suneetha A vs Prem Industries on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160009150/
2 limited to the terms and conditions of the policy.

This respondent denies the very occurrence of the accident and involvement of Eicher, as the same is not within the knowledge of its respondent and the insured in terms of the policy has not intimated the same.
On the date of accident, the Eicher was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of Eicher.
The deceased solely responsible for the accident.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased N. Hemanth Kumar S/o Late.Nanjunde Gowda sustained grievous injury in an accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher bearing No.KA-09- D-8333 on 30-1-2021 at about 7.30 a.m. at Bangalore Mysore road in front of fire service station,
Ramanagara, he succumbed to the said injury?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are legal representatives of the deceased ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, how much and from whom ?
4. What order or award ?
7. The Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1 and.
Ex's .
P1 to 24 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
One L.Rajashekar-Assistant General Manager at NSPIRA Management service private Limited, Bangalore got examined as PW-2 and got marked Ex-P25.
Respondents have not lead either oral or documentary evidence.
8. Arguments were addressed on both side.
9. Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1 :

In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Eicher bearing No.KA-09-D-8333, the petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 24 documents as Ex-P1 to 24 i.e.,FIR, complaint, charge sheet, IMV report, spot mahazar, rough sketch, statement, salary slips, bank statement, PM report, adhar card,
letter dt.24-3-2021, medical bills, adhar card, ER record, receipt identity card, receipt.

3 11.

sentences.text: The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Manjesh Gowda S/o Veeregowda has lodged the complaint as per Ex-P2 before the jurisdictional police.

On the basis of which Ramanagar traffic police conducted a thorough and detailed investigation and filed charge sheet as per Ex-P3 against the driver of the goods carrier/Eicher vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-09-D- 8333 for the offence punishable u/s 279, 304A of IPC by holding that on 30-1-2021 at about 7.30 a.m. accused drove the Eicher vehicle on BM road of Ramanagar, in front of fire station from Mysore in high speed and negligent manner and hit to the Hemanthkumar, pedestrian who was crossing the road and thereby caused the accident.
Due to the impact, Hemanthkumar sustained grievous injuries and succumbed on 7-2-2021 at about 4.00 p.m.
Though respondent counsel seriously disputed the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle but has not examined the driver of the Eicher vehicle to prove his contention.

Respondent counsel cross examined PW-1 at length and it was suggested that deceased Hemanthkumar was crossing the road not on the footpath road and suddenly try to cross the road without observing and noticing the vehicle moving on the road, as such the accident had been taken place which was denied by the PW-1.

Further it was suggested that as the deceased Hemanthkumar suddenly came across the road,
the accident had been taken place due to his rash and negligence and has filed the false complaint.

12. Further, it was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent that the accident had been taken place as the deceased Hemanthkumar came across the road suddenly and as such due to sole negligence of the deceased, the accident had been taken place.

Further it was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that accident had been taken place in the middle of the road and the pedestrian was crossing the road where there was no signal and also no zebra cross and hence percentage of contributory negligence has to be taken into consideration.

In this regard, in the line of arguments, if evidence and documents are perused, on perusal of Ex-P5 and Ex-P6 spot mahazar and sketch, it clearly shows that spot of accident is a Bangalore-Mysore highway road and the accident had been taken place in the middle of the road and there is no zebra cross or any traffic signal for crossing the road.
Thus it appears that accident had been taken place due to some negligence on the part of the deceased also.
13. Now at this juncture, it would be relevant to refer here the judgment rendered in ILR 1998 Kar 1934 between Narasimhaish Vs., The General Manager & Anr.,

entities.text: Narasimhaish Vs., The General Manager & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the pedestrian had crossed the road at a point where he ought not to have crossed the road.
The Hon'ble High Court by observing that petitioner too has contributed negligence has fixed ratio of 40 as negligence contributed by the petitioner.

14. In ILR 1987 Karnataka page 2730 between Sharada Bai Vs. KSRTC., it is held that :
"A driver, particularly of a public transport vehicle, is expected to have a proper look out and provide for the safety of the other users of the road.
In a busy city, a driver must anticipated and provided for the more common follies of other users of the road.

In crowded city roads it is not un often that pedestrians dart across the road,
cyclist and scooterists attempt to weave a zigzag path between other moving vehicles;
school children who are left to fend for themselves, cross the streets unmindful of the hazards of traffic; and all these are a part of the realities of the urban predicament,
Suneetha A vs Prem Industries on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160009150/
4 which any driver, more particularly of a public transport system, ought to be cognizant of.
He must keep his anticipatory reflexes geared to be able to stop the vehicle at a very short notice.

Roads are not meant only for heavy vehicles; they are also meant for other users of the road and the drivers of heavy vehicles must negotiate their vehicles in such a way as not to jeopardise the safety of the other users of the road".

"If the tortfeasor's negligence or breach of duty is established as causative of the damage, the onus is on him to establish that the victim's contributory negligence was a substantial or cooperating cause.

In order to establish the defence of contributory negligence the propounder of that defence must prove, first, that the victim failed to take reasonable care of himself or, in other words, such care as a man of ordinary prudence would have done and that was a contributory cause of the accident.
The amount of care which a person could reasonably be expected to take, must needs vary with the circumstances and conditions actually prevailing at the material point of time.
However, it is relevant to note that, in order to discharge of burden of proof, it is unnecessary for the propounder of that defence to adduce evidence about the matter.

Contributory negligence can be and very often is inferred from the evidence already adduced on the claimants behalf or from the perceptive facts, either admitted or found established, on a balance of probabilities in the case".

15. In unreported judgment rendered in MFA No. 7070/2015 (MV) between Smt.Mina Limbu &
Ors., Vs., M/s Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd., it was held by referring the facts of the case that "pedestrian crossing the road at a point where he ought not to have done, it has to be considered that pedestrian too has contributed negligence.

entities.text:
Smt.Mina Limbu &
Ors., Vs., M/s Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, 25% of negligence was attributed against the deceased.

16. In MFA NO.2380/2016 between Smt. Gangamma Vs., Sri. Vardharaju & Anr., in the said case also referring some of the judgment rendered by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it has observed that "where the person is crossing the road where there was no zebra crossing and accident occurs,
some percentage of negligence has to be attributed against the person who crossed the road and met with an accident".

entities.text: Smt. Gangamma Vs., Sri. Vardharaju & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, 20% negligence was attributed against the deceased.

17. Further in MFA No.No.2613/2010 Smt.N.Bharathamma & Ors., Vs. Mr.Syed Masood Matheen &
Anr., in the said case also by observing that deceased has contributed 25% to the occurrence and in the said case also the deceased while crossing the road had met with an accident.
18. If spot mahazar is perused, the spot of accident is a curve road and accident had taken place in middle of the road.

entities.text:
MFA No.No.2613/2010 Smt.N.Bharathamma & Ors., Vs. Mr.Syed Masood Matheen &
Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When the spot of accident is National High way and is a curve road and when deceased has already crossed the road and was in the middle of the road, if the driver of the offending vehicle had driven his vehicle in moderate speed with care and caution he could have control over the vehicle on seeing the deceased crossing the road and in such circumstances he could have avoided the accident.

Hence, by taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case it can be said that the driver of the offending vehicle has contributed negligence to an extent of Suneetha A vs Prem Industries on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160009150/
5 80% and deceased to an extent of 20%.

entities.text: Suneetha A vs Prem Industries on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As the deceased has contributed negligence to an extent of 20% the petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 20%.
19.

Since both deceased and respondent No.2 had contributed negligence to an extent of 20 : 80,
this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 20%.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to pay 80% of the awarded compensation to the petitioners.
80% of the compensation shall carry interest at 6% p.a.
Accordingly issue No.1 in the partly affirmative

. 
20. ISSUES NO.2 & 3 :
The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed that petitioner No.1 is his mother, petitioner No.2 is her son.
The petitioners have produced Ex-P16, 17 and Ex-P20-Adhaar card of petitioner No.1 and 2 and deceased Hemanth Kumar.
The documents which are exhibited at Ex's.P16, 17 and 20 reveals the aforesaid relationship of the claimants with the deceased Hemanth Kumar.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents, as it is evident from the tenor of cross-examination of PW.1.

Be that as it may, since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.

Under such circumstances it is clear that petitioners No.1 and 2 are are entitled for the compensation.
21. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:

The petitioners have produced Ex-P20-Adhar card which reveals the age of the deceased Hemanth Kumar is shown as 21-11-1978 and as on the date of accident i.e., on 30-1-2021, the age of the deceased is 43 years.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group of 41 to 45 is '14'.
22.

According to PW.1, the deceased Hemanth Kumar was working at Narayana Olympiad school,
Saraswathi Bhavan branch, Bangalore and earning Rs.28,179/- p.m.
The petitioners have produced Ex-P9 and 10-salary slips which relates to the month of March 2020.
Further produced bank statement Ex-P13 and 14 which pertaining to the year 2019-2020.

23. Later on petitioner examined one L.Rajashekar- Assistant General Manager at H.R.Department,
NSPIRA Management services private limited, Bangalore as PW-2 wherein PW-2 has clearly deposed that the deceased Hemanthkumar has joined the service in the company on 26- 3-2015 and worked till 21-1-2021 and at that time, he was drawing salary of Rs.28,179/-.

entities.text:
H.R.Department,
NSPIRA Management services private limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further PW-2 has produced extract copy of the salary acquittance register of the deceased Hemanthkumar from 2015 to May 2020.
Further PW-2 has given the clarification that since there was a Covid in 2020 May, the school was closed and hence he has not given the salary from May 2020 to the deceased Hemanthkumar.
Even though PW-2 was cross examined and it was suggested that from May 2020 till January 2021, deceased was not working in their school for which PW-2 has outrightly denied the said suggestion.

Admittedly though except Ex-P25, the petitioner has not produced any document to show that deceased was working in the NSPIRA Naryana Olympied school as on the date of accident, but has deposed by the PW-2 and has rightly argued by the petitioner counsel,
admittedly there was covid 19 from March 2020 till February 2022 and admittedly deceased was working as Warden in the NSPIR Narayana Olympied school and admittedly as stated by PW-2,
Suneetha A vs Prem Industries on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160009150/
6 hostels and schools were closed during the covid period and this court can take judicial notice of covid period, closure and lockdown period and by considering that the deceased was working as a warden and drawing salary of Rs.28,179/- as per Ex-P25 and since there was a closure and lock down due to covid-19 period, salary was not given to the deceased from May 2020 till the date of accident.

In view of all the above discussions and reasons, it can be considered that deceased was working as a Warden at NSPIRA Narayana Olympied school as on the date of accident and drawing salary of Rs.28,179/-.

Hence income of the deceased is taken as Rs.28,179/-p.m.
24.

In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others),
the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in the absence of proof of income.

entities.text: 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand the deceased was aged 43 years.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SCC 5157,
30% of income is to be added towards future prospects in case of salaried person.
30% of Rs.28,179/- works out to Rs.8,454/-.

Therefore the total income comes to Rs.36,633/-
(28,179+8454).

Admittedly, the deceased was bachelor and as such in view of the proposition of Law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma's case, half of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/2 of Rs.36633/- works out to Rs.18317/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.18317/- (36633- 18317).
Annual income works out to Rs.2,19,804/- (18317 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '14'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.30,77,256/- (2,19,804 X 14).
25. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/- (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.40,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) on account of loss of spousal consortium, parental consortium and loss of love & affection.
26. LOSS OF ESTATE:

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards loss of estate.

27. FUNERAL EXPENSES: Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards funeral expenses.

28. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of Dependency : 30,77,256-00 2 Loss of Consortium : 96,800-00 3 Loss of Estate : 18,150-00 4 Funeral Expenses : 18,150-00 Total Rs.32,10,356=00

Hence,
petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.32,10,356/-.
29. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

30. Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the Suneetha A vs Prem Industries on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160009150/
7 petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

31. Since both deceased and respondent No.2 had contributed negligence to an extent of 20 : 80,
this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 20%.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to pay 80% of the awarded compensation to the petitioners.
80% of the compensation shall carry interest at 6% p.a.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative' and issue No.3 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
32. ISSUE NO.4 :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,68,285/- (80% of Rs.32,10,356/-) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 80- %
 Petitioner No.2 20 - %
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 and 2 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

When the spot of accident is National High way and is a curve road and when deceased has already crossed the road and was in the middle of the road, if the driver of the offending vehicle had driven his vehicle in moderate speed with care and caution he could have control over the vehicle on seeing the deceased crossing the road and in such circumstances he could have avoided the accident.
As the deceased has contributed negligence to an extent of 20% the petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 20%.
19.
Since both deceased and respondent No.2 had contributed negligence to an extent of 20 : 80,
this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 20%.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
